messages.subject: Detect objects by shape or sourrinding color?
messages.subject_clean: Detect objects by shape or sourrinding color?
messages.body_plain:
Hello community, thanks for letting me into this group.

I have a simple question: is it possible to filter objects by their surrounding color? Unfortunately I can't use the function "fieldMask", because the colors appear more often in the image and I would eliminate my objects with it. I would have to identify the objects by either the shape or the enclosing color. Does FieldImageR provide a way to do this?

Thanks, happy new year and best regards
Florian

messages.subject: In fieldIndex NAs produced by integer overflow
messages.subject_clean: In fieldIndex NAs produced by integer overflow
messages.body_plain:
Hi Filipe,

I've been having issues extracting VI information from my RGB orthomosaics. I run fieldIndex and will get this warning message:

In getValues(e1) * getValues(e2) : NAs produced by integer overflow

It still extracts data and I can create a datasheet, however, many of the values for VARI and BGI are labeled NA, inf, or -inf. The remaining VIs all seem to work as does the individual band extraction. The same issue occurs when I run the same code on my multispectral orthomosaics. Is there maybe a way to increase the integer length in the code or reduce the integer length in the analysis?

Thanks!

Eric

messages.subject: Re: Detect objects by shape or sourrinding color?
messages.subject_clean: Detect objects by shape or sourrinding color?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Florian,

Thanks for contacting us. Right now, FIELDimageR only works with image segmentation using the entire image. We did not implement any type of strategy (e.g. traditional machine learning models for example) for specific selections of shapes as you suggested. One possibility is to use the function fieldPolygon (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P15) to select your object's boundaries and use these new polygons-shapefiles to extract information. Is that make sense?

Hope someone else here in the community helps us to figure it out... For instance, sharing one example/sample (image) from your dataset explaining exactly what you are looking for can help us to visualize your needs.

Please, let us know if you develop any new strategy or have ideas about what to do... ok.

All the best,
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: In fieldIndex NAs produced by integer overflow
messages.subject_clean: In fieldIndex NAs produced by integer overflow
messages.body_plain:
Hi Eric,

Thanks for asking. I am not sure why this is happening. I have some questions: (1) Are you removing the soil? (2) Did you check if there is any plot without pixels after removing the soil that may be causing this error? Did you check if there are any strange pixel values at the same location of those plots with errors in the image (for example reflective GCPs or paper, etc that may reflect more and cause this error)?

Could you share an image and shapefile to be able to replicate the error and check the function?

Thanks a lot,
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: Orthomosaic size reduction or orthomosaic preparation prior to import in R
messages.subject_clean: Orthomosaic size reduction or orthomosaic preparation prior to import in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Thanks for contacting us. Unfortunately R was not made for large and havier images as yours seem. But I believe you can evaluate some strategies as (1) increasing the R base memory following this link (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P20), (2) reducing resolution size (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P12), or even (3) working with single and individual images before making the large and heavier orthomosaic. In this last case, you can use the GPS location to identify from each plot the information or counting is coming from (I never did this before and I believe this strategy only works for Drones with RTK).

Let's see if someone here in the community has any other idea to help us.

Thanks,
Filipe
